fullPassage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the patch to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.

❌ ③ fundamentally — 근본적으로 (동의어)
✅ ④ externally — 외부적으로 ←정답 (반의어)
det.tip: inherently(본질적으로, 내재적으로) ↔ externally(외부적으로)

questions.passage: The concept of ecosystem states should be familiar to anyone with a home vegetable garden. The garden is a small ecosystem that the grower attempts to keep in a specific state, namely the maximization of fruit and vegetable production. To achieve this, the grower is almost always intervening in the dynamics of the ecosystem; they remove unwanted plants that begin to grow and perhaps spray insecticides and fence off the <u>patch</u> to stop insects and other animals from consuming the vegetables. Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is effectively keeping the ball on a slope. If the grower stops intervening, even for a day, the ecosystem, that small patch of ground, will naturally begin to shift to a more stable state. Vegetables may still grow, but yield will almost certainly be lower as other plants crowd out the vegetables and wildlife consume the produce.
questions.stem: 다음 밑줄 친 단어 patch가 (A)와 (B)에서 각각 어떤 의미로 쓰였는지 고르시오.

det.korean: (A) patch = (땅의) 구역, 일부분 / (B) patch = 수선하다, 기우다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 붙이다는 동사 의미. (A)에서 patch는 명사(구역)
✅ ② (A) 구역 — (B) 수선하다: (A)에서 patch는 채소밭의 '구역'을, (B)에서는 재킷 구멍을 '수선하다'의 의미 ←정답
❌ ③ (A)는 수선하다가 아닌 구역
❌ ④ (B)는 붙이다가 아닌 수선하다
det.tip: patch: 명사 = 구역, 조각 / 동사 = 수선하다, 붙이다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the process of making something as large or great as possible"

det.korean: 무언가를 가능한 한 크게 또는 위대하게 만드는 과정 = maximization(극대화)
det.analysis:
❌ ① minimization — 최소화 (반의어)
❌ ② stabilization — 안정화 (무관)
✅ ③ maximization — 극대화 ←정답
❌ ④ production — 생산 (유사하나 '극대화'의 의미 아님)
det.tip: maximization = 극대화. maximize의 명사형

questions.passage: The grower sprays insecticides and fences off the patch to stop insects and other animals from __________ (consume) the vegetables.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 재배자는 곤충과 다른 동물이 채소를 먹는 것을 막기 위해 살충제를 뿌리고 울타리를 친다
det.analysis: from + V-ing 구문. 전치사 from 뒤에는 동명사(V-ing)가 온다. consume → consuming
det.tip: stop/prevent/keep ~ from V-ing: ~가 ...하는 것을 막다

questions.passage: Since maximizing vegetable growth is an inherently unstable state for the ecosystem, the grower is __________ (effective) keeping the ball on a slope.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (   ) 쓰시오. (영어로)

det.korean: 채소 성장을 극대화하는 것은 본질적으로 불안정한 상태이므로, 재배자는 사실상 공을 경사면 위에 올려놓고 있는 것이다

det.tip: 형용사 → 부사: effective(효과적인) → effectively(효과적으로, 사실상)
